newsitem.title: UK: UK's Carlton drops despite profit rise.
newsitem.headline: UK's Carlton drops despite profit rise.

text.p: Shares in British media company Carlton Communications Plc were dragged down on Wednesday by a falling FTSE 100 in early trading, despite results confirming a hearty 20 percent rise in pre-tax profits, analysts said.
"All the businesses are firing on all cylinders," said UBS media analyst Colin Tennant. "They're a solid set of figures and the outlook for the next year is encouraging," he added.
But by 0950 GMT, the shares were down eight pence at 495.5p.
"The market is moving off anyway," said SGST media analyst Jason Crisp. "There's nothing really for people to grab on to," he added.
Carlton posted annual pre-tax profits of 295.1 million stg, in line with analysts forecasts, compared with 246.7 million stg last year.
Despite strength in most of Carlton's core businesses and rising advertising yields, analysts said the shares were hit by a slight downtrend in the FTSE 100.
The Dow's sharp decline overnight dragged 80 percent of top FTSE blue-chips lower on Wednesday.
